Thus the reduced denominators of ax+1 and bx+1 are v/d_a and v/d_b. A reduced rational square has square numerator and denominator, including when the numerator is zero, giving the displayed denominator and numerator square identities."},{"location":"Proof, reduction modulo p","explanation":"The condition e>max(alpha,beta) implies p divides v but not u, and v_p(d_a)=alpha and v_p(d_b)=beta. Dividing the numerator identities by p^alpha and p^beta and reducing modulo p eliminates the v terms. The resulting nonzero left sides also ensure A_1 and B_1 are nonzero modulo p, so taking their ratio is valid."},{"location":"Proof, denominator ratio and conclusion","explanation":"From v=d_a r^2=d_b s^2, d_b/d_a=r^2/s^2. Comparing p-adic valuations yields beta-alpha=2v_p(r/s), and hence d_{b,0}/d_{a,0}=((r/s)/p^k)^2 for k=v_p(r/s). This is a p-adic unit square; the ratio congruence therefore implies that a_0/b_0 is a nonzero square modulo p. The stated contrapositive follows."}],"citation_checks":[],"external_dependency_coverage":{"complete":true,"undeclared_external_results":[]}}]}}
